name: CounterLabel
statusNote: CounterLabel ships on every tab and button with a count on GitHub; alpha is Primer's label. The scheme prop is a deprecated alias of variant.
summary: A small pill showing a count next to a tab, button or heading. Choose secondary (the default) for ordinary counts and primary for one that needs attention; inside a Button, the button supplies the colours.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: The text shown (children), normally a number already formatted by the caller ("5", "1.2k"). Empty hides the pill.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Emphasis: secondary is a pale neutral pill with default text, primary a dark neutral pill with onEmphasis text.

anatomy.name: Pill
anatomy.description: An inline box with 2px vertical and 6px horizontal padding, a 1px --counter-borderColor border (transparent in standard themes) and 20px corner radius.

anatomy.name: Text
anatomy.description: The count at the small body size, semibold, line height 1.

anatomy.name: Spoken label
anatomy.description: Visually hidden text " (count)" after the pill; the pill itself is hidden from assistive technology.

layout.text: The pill is inline-block: 2px top and bottom and 6px side padding, plus a 1px border, around a line box exactly one font size tall; at 12px text it is 18px tall.
Corners are a hard-coded 20px radius, more than half the 18px height, so the ends are fully round.
Width hugs the text with no minimum, so a single digit makes a pill about 20px wide rather than a circle.
An empty count removes the pill from layout entirely.

states.text: Static: the variant's fill and text colour with the --counter-borderColor border. It has no interactive states of its own.

states.label: in-button
states.text: Inside a Button the button overrides the pill's colours with its variant's --buttonCounter-* tokens, and a disabled or inactive button makes the text inherit its colour; see button.

behaviour.text: Display the count exactly as given; the component neither formats nor caps numbers (99+ and 1.2k are the caller's job).
Variant falls back to the deprecated scheme, then to secondary.

semantics: The visible pill is aria-hidden; screen readers read the hidden text " (5)" instead, so a count after a label reads as "Issues (5)".
Nothing announces a change in the count; a live count needs a caller-supplied live region.

notes.text: The hidden spoken label is rendered even when the count is empty, so a hidden pill still reads as " ()". A native build should omit the spoken label with the pill.

--counter-borderColor is transparent in standard and colourblind themes and a visible grey in the high-contrast themes, where the pill gains a real outline. The 1px border is always part of the box, so the pill's size does not change between themes.
The 20px radius and line-height 1 are hard-coded rather than read from --borderRadius-full and a type token.
Empty means no text at all; the count 0 is text and shows a "0" pill. Hide a zero count by passing nothing.
The spoken form relies on a visually hidden sibling span with a leading non-breaking space; a native build sets the accessible text of the owning control (tab, button) to include "(count)" instead.
